_doc: Read by gate 2b of the door (`src/mcgyvr/serving/gate-scripts/02-rig.py`). srv1-multi-gpu measures srv1 with two cards in it: what the link between them is (1-link), the vLLM checkpoints put in the HF cache (2-fetch), vLLM on one card, tensor-parallel, pipeline-parallel and as two replicas, with NCCL peer access on and off (3-vllm), llama-server on one card, layer split, row split and as two replicas (4-lcp), llama-bench across the same splits (5-lcp-bench), vLLM on a checkpoint under ~/models (6-local), NCCL settings on the bare collective plus host-memory and dual-H2D bandwidth (7-nccl), vLLM and llama.cpp settings held one at a time under sustained load (8-vknobs, 9-lknobs), llama-bench over batch, KV type and depth (10-bench), the model axis on llama.cpp (11-ladder) and vLLM (12-vladder), long windows (13-vctx, 14-lctx), vLLM's scheduler and n-gram speculation (15-vsched), the PCIe links held to gen3/2/1 (16-pcie), and further architectures and speculative decoding (17-arch), MoE experts held in host RAM (18-offload), the pair with peer access (Resizable BAR plus the P2P-patched open kernel module at the same driver version) on the cells of steps 1, 7, 8 and 9, refusing to write a row unless peer access is live (19-p2p), step 1's link probe with BAR1 resized and the stock driver (20-rebar), and the all-reduce with NCCL told to take the peer path (21-nccl-sys). Every step reads and files both cards' identity, because hosts.json describes one. It drives containers through tools/runs/drivers/mgpu_sweep.py and never the serving harness, so it is not held to that harness's markers.
